result:
I fixed the 10 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings. A check script compared all 150 rules against what their docstrings say (qty 0–299 across several unit prices), and after the fixes every rule matches.

| Rule | What it did | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 35 | Rounded the discount with `round()`, but the common rule says round down | Changed to `// 100` (round down) |
| 37 | Only applied the 100,000 won cap when the discount was over 200,000 | Always applies the cap |
| 67 | Docstring says "marginal" but it discounted the whole amount | Discounts only the units above 10 |
| 89 | Discount started at 11 units, docstring says 10 | Starts at 10 |
| 90 | Took 11% off, docstring says 10% | 10% |
| 103 | Docstring says "whole" but it discounted only the units above 30 | Discounts the whole amount |
| 115 | Discount started at 6 units, docstring says 5 | Starts at 5 |
| 136 | Took 6% off, docstring says 5% | 5% |
| 146 | Capped the price at 30,000 won instead of the discount | Caps the discount |
| 149 | Took 8% off, docstring says 7% | 7% |

I also changed rule 148's start from `qty >= 11` to `>= 10` to match its docstring. This doesn't change any result: at exactly 10 units the marginal discount is 0 anyway.

STATUS: DONE
